title: List of Forms and Contact Details Required to Request Medical Records From NewYork-Presbyterian
summary: How to request medical records from NewYork-Presbyterian: the centralized ROI process, authorization requirements, facility contacts, and how Codes Health returns records in a couple of weeks on a flat fee.
body_markdown:
NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital includes eight hospital campuses, while the broader NewYork-Presbyterian system encompasses 10 hospitals and hundreds of locations across the Greater New York area. For personal injury attorneys handling medical litigation, getting complete records from a system that size means navigating a centralized request process, facility-specific contacts, and strict authorization requirements. Missing a single set of initials on the form can cost you weeks.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) offers AI-assisted retrieval that catches those errors before submission, validates authorizations, and manages persistent follow-up, working toward complete records in a couple of weeks.


## **Key Takeaways**


-


NewYork-Presbyterian uses a centralized Release of Information call center at 646-697-4764, also styled 646-NYP-4ROI, available Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m.


-


The NYP authorization requires separate initials when records contain alcohol or drug treatment, mental health treatment other than psychotherapy notes, HIV/AIDS-related information, or genetic testing information


-


NYP states that submitted medical record requests will be fulfilled within 10 business days


-


New York law permits hospitals to charge up to $0.75 per page in applicable circumstances, though HIPAA right-of-access requests are subject to federal reasonable, cost-based limits


-


NYP states that subpoenas are not accepted through its online attorney authorization method, and that using it does not constitute proper service


-


[Codes Health's AI review](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) flags authorization issues before submission, working toward records in a couple of weeks on a flat fee


## **Understanding the NYP Records Request Process**


NewYork-Presbyterian routes hospital record requests through its Medical Correspondence Units. NYP's current medical records contact page groups Columbia University Irving Medical Center, Morgan Stanley Children's Hospital, and Allen Hospital under one contact, and separately lists Weill Cornell Medical Center, Lower Manhattan, Westchester Behavioral Health Center, Hudson Valley Hospital, Brooklyn Methodist Hospital, Queens, and Westchester.


The hospital offers[three primary request](https://www.nyp.org/patients-visitors/medical-records) methods:


-


**Connect patient portal** , which provides immediate access to records already available in the portal, with no fee when records are released to Connect


-


**Online digital authorization submission** for patients, representatives, and attorneys, in English, Spanish, and Chinese


-


**Paper authorization forms** , submitted using the current instructions on NYP's medical records page. NYP publishes an email submission option and facility-specific mailing addresses


For legal teams, the key distinction is which method applies to attorney requests versus patient-directed requests. Attorney requests need a patient-signed authorization naming the law firm as recipient. The online submission is available to attorneys, but subpoenas follow a different process entirely.


NYP states that submitted requests will be fulfilled within 10 business days. Real timelines can run longer once rejections, resubmissions, and multi-campus coordination enter the picture.


## **HIPAA and the NYP Authorization Form**


NewYork-Presbyterian uses an Authorization to Disclose Protected Health Information form that meets HIPAA requirements under 45 C.F.R. § 164.508 and includes NYP-specific fields a generic form may lack.


### **Key Sections of the Form**


-


Patient name, date of birth, and current address


-


Recipient information specifying who receives the records


-


Specific records requested, with the dates of service the form requires


-


The expiration provision. NYP's form states it expires one year after signing unless a shorter expiration date is entered, so a manually written date is not always required


-


Patient signature and date


-


**Sensitive information initials** for alcohol or drug treatment, mental health treatment other than psychotherapy notes, HIV/AIDS-related information, and genetic testing information


Failure to initial an applicable sensitive-information category can prevent those records from being released. That is worth flagging to the client at signature, because the rest of the chart arrives looking complete while the withheld portion is exactly the part a psychological injury claim depends on. Missing initials can require a corrected authorization, which adds delay.


### **Who Can Request Records**


Authorized requestors include the patient, legal representatives with a documented relationship, attorneys with a patient-signed authorization naming the firm, healthcare providers for treatment purposes, and insurance companies with proper authorization.


For attorneys, the authorization must specifically name the firm or attorney as recipient. Language directing records to "my attorney" without identifying information can cause processing delays.


Codes Health states that its e-signature workflow is HIPAA-compliant, and its[validation catches](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) missing signatures, uninitialed sensitive-information categories, and unclear expiration provisions before submission.


## **Step-by-Step: Requesting NYP Records**


-


**Step 1: Get the correct form.** Download the current version from the[NYP medical records](https://www.nyp.org/patients-visitors/medical-records) page. Forms are available in English, Spanish, and Chinese. A generic HIPAA form instead of the NYP version can cause delays.


-


**Step 2: Complete every field.** Full patient identifying information, specific date ranges, the expiration provision, initials on all applicable sensitive-information categories, and signature with date.


-


**Step 3: Identify the correct facility.** Determine which campus or campuses provided care, and check whether your request routes through one contact grouping or needs separate submissions.


-


**Step 4: Submit through the right channel.** Use the online submission portal, or send the completed paper authorization to the email address listed on NYP's official medical records page. Mailing addresses are published by facility on the contact page.


-


**Step 5: Track and follow up.** Online submissions allow status tracking through the portal. Otherwise, call the centralized ROI number at 646-697-4764 and follow the current prompts for the applicable facility.


If your request is delayed, common causes are missing or incomplete fields, uninitialed sensitive-information categories, incorrect facility routing, and unclear date ranges. Contact the ROI call center to identify the specific issue and submit a corrected authorization.


## **NYP Contact Information**


### **Centralized Release of Information**


**Primary ROI number** : 646-697-4764 (646-NYP-4ROI), Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. Follow the current prompts for the applicable facility rather than relying on a published menu sequence, since phone trees change.


**Westchester Behavioral Health Center** : 914-997-5988 for AOT, subpoenas, and outpatient department requests. NYP also lists 646-697-4764 for this facility.


**Office of Legal Affairs & Risk Management** : 212-305-1919 for service-of-process questions.


### **Submitting Completed Forms**


Submit the completed paper authorization to the email address listed on NYP's official medical records page. For mail, addresses vary by facility and are published on the[contact and locations](https://www.nyp.org/patients-visitors/medical-records/contact-locations) page, which also provides phone extensions and in-person pickup information.


**Physician office records require separate requests** to outpatient record departments:


-


**ColumbiaDoctors outpatient records** : 212-305-8255, ColumbiaDoctors-HIM@cumc.columbia.edu


-


**Weill Cornell Medicine outpatient records** : 646-962-9820, medicalrecords@med.cornell.edu, fax 646-962-0635


Codes Health manages provider outreach across calls, faxes, emails, and portals, which removes the need to track separate submissions and follow-up schedules for each campus and practice.


## **Requesting Specific Record Types**


### **Billing Records**


Billing records drive damages calculations but may not come with a standard clinical release. Specify billing records explicitly on the authorization along with the relevant date ranges. Clarity in the request is what prevents partial fulfillment.


### **Imaging and Pathology**


Radiology films or images require special handling. For same-day or walk-in film requests, contact the facility's[radiology department](https://www.nyp.org/patients-visitors/medical-records/contact-locations) directly. For other film requests, NYP directs users to the centralized ROI process. Radiology reports can be specifically requested on the medical record authorization.


Worth being precise here: NYP provides facility-specific contacts for same-day or walk-in radiology-film service. That is not a same-day retrieval service for the broader chart.


Pathology slides are handled through facility-specific pathology departments, with their own procedures and timelines.


For cases needing comprehensive documentation, firms often submit multiple requests to different departments within the same system.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) coordinates these through a single platform, tracking each component until the record set is assembled.


## **The Connect Patient Portal**


Connect provides immediate access to records already available in the portal, and NYP states that no fee applies when records are released to Connect. Patients may request additional records for upload to the portal's Document Center, and those requested records are not necessarily fulfilled immediately.


Registration is available through NYP's patient portal page. Once registered, patients can view available records, download copies, request records not yet in the portal, and set up proxy access for authorized representatives.


Not all records may already appear in Connect. If expected records are missing, confirm the treatment occurred at an NYP facility rather than an affiliated but separate practice, check the portal's available date range, and submit a formal request for anything outside it.


For legal purposes, portal access is a useful starting point but rarely captures the complete record set needed for case evaluation.


## **Retrieving Older Records**


### **Retention**


New York hospital regulations under 10 NYCRR § 405.10 require hospital medical records to be retained for at least six years from discharge, subject to longer retention rules for minors and certain other circumstances. For minors, records must be kept at least six years from discharge or three years after the patient reaches age 18, whichever is longer.


Records beyond these periods may still exist in archived systems but are not guaranteed. When requesting older records, specify approximate treatment dates and prepare for the possibility that some materials are gone.


### **Archived Materials**


Archived records may take additional processing time while facilities retrieve materials from off-site storage or legacy systems. Submit these requests early in the case timeline, include any documentation that helps identify the specific records, and follow up specifically about archived availability.


Codes Health uses provider and facility data to help identify where records may exist, which matters most for long medical histories or incomplete client recollection about treatment locations.


### **Deceased Patients**


For a deceased patient, NYP instructs requesters to contact the applicable Medical Correspondence Unit. NYP may require a death certificate and documentation establishing the requester's status as next of kin, executor, distributee, or other authorized representative, with the authorization signed according to the applicable hierarchy.


## **Ensuring Completeness**


Receiving records does not mean receiving complete records.


**Review each delivery for** :


-


Missing date ranges, compared against the treatment dates your client reports


-


Absent billing records, where clinical records arrived without corresponding billing


-


Missing facility records, since multi-campus treatment can produce partial responses


-


Absent imaging, where you have radiology interpretations but not the underlying films


-


Withheld sensitive information, where an uninitialed category kept mental health or substance use records out of the set


When records appear incomplete, document specifically what is missing against the original request, contact the ROI department about the missing materials, determine whether they require a new request or can be fulfilled under the existing authorization, and submit a corrected authorization if uninitialed categories were the problem.


[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) checks delivered records against the original request before closing retrieval, and works with the facility to resolve identified gaps.


## **Attorney-Specific Considerations**


Attorney requests differ from patient requests in several ways:


-


**Authorization** : must specifically name the law firm as recipient


-


**Fees** : attorney-request fees can depend on the legal mechanism used. A patient-directed HIPAA access request may be subject to HIPAA's cost-based fee limits under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524(c)(4), while a separate third-party authorization or other legal process can be treated differently. New York law permits up to $0.75 per page in applicable circumstances


-


**Subpoenas** : NYP states that subpoenas are not accepted through its online attorney medical record authorization submission method, and that using that method does not constitute proper service. For service-of-process questions, contact the Office of Legal Affairs & Risk Management at 212-305-1919


-


**Identity documentation** : some electronic workflows may require it. NYP's FAQ states that users of the Verisma portal should have two forms of picture identification available to scan

## **The Bottom Line for Firms Requesting NYP Records**


Most delays on NYP requests are not bad luck. They are preventable failure modes that repeat until the process changes.


The first is the initials omission. The sensitive-information categories require separate initials, and leaving one blank produces a record set that looks complete until you notice the behavioral health portion never arrived.


The second is the routing error. ColumbiaDoctors and Weill Cornell outpatient records run through their own departments, and a hospital request will not reach them. Radiology films and pathology slides have their own procedures too.


The third is the subpoena assumption. NYP says its online attorney authorization method is not proper service, so a subpoena sent that way has not been served at all.


The fourth is mistaking delivery for completeness, which surfaces during trial prep when the billing file or one campus's records turn out never to have arrived.


Each is fixable in advance. Address every applicable sensitive-information category at signature. Confirm which department holds the records you need. Use the correct channel for subpoenas. And check what came back against what you asked for.

## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **How long does it take to receive records from NewYork-Presbyterian?**


NYP states that submitted medical record requests will be fulfilled within 10 business days. Actual timelines for law firms often run longer once authorization corrections, resubmissions, and multi-campus coordination are factored in, and a request needing a corrected authorization for uninitialed sensitive-information categories adds delay each time.[Codes Health](https://www.getcodeshealth.com/) reports a typical turnaround of a couple of weeks.


### **Can I request records for a deceased family member?**


Yes, with documentation. NYP instructs requesters to contact the applicable Medical Correspondence Unit and may require a death certificate along with documentation establishing status as next of kin, executor, distributee, or other authorized representative, with the authorization signed according to the applicable hierarchy. Call 646-697-4764 for the specific requirements.


### **Is there a fee for NYP records?**


It depends on format and requestor. There is no fee when records are released to the Connect portal. New York law permits hospitals to charge up to $0.75 per page in applicable circumstances. For a request under an individual's HIPAA right of access, federal law limits charges to a reasonable, cost-based fee under 45 C.F.R. § 164.524(c)(4). Attorney-request fees depend on the legal mechanism used.


### **What if my records come back incomplete?**


Document exactly what is missing against your original request and known treatment dates, then contact the ROI department to determine whether the missing items can be provided under the existing authorization or need a new one. Common causes are uninitialed sensitive-information categories, separate facility or outpatient department records, and radiology films or pathology slides requiring direct department contact.


### **Can an attorney request records directly from NYP?**


Yes, with a patient-signed authorization specifically naming the attorney or firm as recipient. Generic authorizations directing records to "my attorney" can cause delays. For subpoenas, NYP states its online attorney authorization method is not accepted as proper service, so contact the Office of Legal Affairs & Risk Management at 212-305-1919.


### **How far back can NYP provide records?**


New York hospital regulations require records to be retained for at least six years from discharge, with a longer rule for minors of three years after the patient reaches age 18, whichever is longer. Records beyond those periods may exist in archives but are not guaranteed. Specify approximate treatment dates and allow extra time for retrieval from archived systems.
